name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Bank Indonesia raised rates to 6% on 18 Nov to support the rupiah near record lows; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: Bank Indonesia unexpectedly raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 points to 6% on 18 Nov and stepped up currency intervention, with the rupiah at about 18,245 per dollar, down 0.66% since end-Oct (Malay Mail). The rupiah briefly touched a record near 18,290 on 17 Nov amid political uncertainty after the vice-president's resignation (Trading Economics). It has not fallen 10% in a month, reserves stood at $146.8bn, and no major emerging economy in default, under capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 18 Nov.
for_you: People and firms in Indonesia face higher borrowing costs and import prices. Elsewhere, emerging-market stress is contained for now, with no default or emergency IMF programme in a major economy.
rubric_hit: Normal: rupiah down 0.66% since end-Oct, below the 10%-in-a-month Watch line; no IMF request, default or capital controls

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
